text:
Jenna Park: hey folks — first-day kube hiccup. I ran the onboarding script and it wrote my kubeconfig but when I switch to redwood-staging the namespace seems to still be default. `kubectl config use-context redwood-staging` shows no error but `kubectl get pods` returns pods from default ns. any quick checks? @Marc (infra) @Sasha (devex)
Marc (infra): welcome! quick thing: do you have KUBECONFIG env set or are you using our sso helper? sometimes the onboarding script writes ~/.kube/config but KUBECONFIG points elsewhere so kubectl reads a different file
Jenna Park: I used ./scripts/get-kube.sh which printed "wrote kubeconfig to ~/.kube/config". I didn't think to check env var.
Sasha (devex): hey jenna — happy to help. two quick approaches: 1) unset KUBECONFIG and re-run `kubectl config use-context redwood-staging` or 2) explicitly set the namespace on the context: `kubectl config set-context redwood-staging --namespace=team-ml` — onboarding intentionally leaves namespace blank for safety
Jenna Park: here's output I pasted:
```
$ kubectl config get-contexts
CURRENT   NAME               CLUSTER          AUTHINFO          NAMESPACE
*         redwood-staging    redwood-1        jenna@redwood
```
So NAMESPACE column is empty even though current is redwood-staging.
Marc (infra): yep that means the context doesn't have a namespace set. `kubectl get pods` uses default unless you pass -n. Also double-check `echo $KUBECONFIG` — if it's set to something else you'll be reading a different file
Jenna Park: aargh I do have `KUBECONFIG=/tmp/kc` from a local test. that explains it 🤦‍♀️
Jenna Park: unset KUBECONFIG; re-ran `kubectl config use-context redwood-staging`; `kubectl get pods -n team-ml` now shows the expected pods
Sasha (devex): nice! I'll add a short note to the new-hire checklist to remind folks to clear KUBECONFIG or export the path. thanks for catching this — super common
Devex Bot: :pushpin: onboarding checklist updated by Sasha (devex)
Marc (infra): if you prefer context to always default to team-ml run: `kubectl config set-context redwood-staging --namespace=team-ml` — saves needing -n all the time. Also for long-term, we can add context namespace in the kubeconfig we hand out if the team requests
Jenna Park: one follow-up: who do I ping for RBAC access to read secrets in team-ml? file a support ticket or ping infra?
Marc (infra): open a ticket in #support with the RBAC tag and include your team, the service account you need, and which secrets. For secrets read access we need SRE approval and an acl entry. you can also ping me directly if you want faster triage
Jenna Park: will file the ticket now. really appreciate the fast help — thanks everyone :tada:
